about.title: Perris Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Perris sits at a working crossroads of Riverside County, where warehouses, distribution yards, construction sites and farm operations keep a lot of people on their feet, on ladders, and behind the wheel every shift. When one of those shifts ends in an injury, the path forward is not always obvious. Workers' compensation covers most job injuries in California no matter who was at fault, and it is usually the only claim you can bring against your own employer. Still, that is not the whole picture. If a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of a defective forklift or press, or another driver caused the harm, a separate third-party claim may exist alongside your comp benefits. That matters here: Perris recorded 267 injury collisions in 2025, and anyone hurt in a work vehicle on Perris Boulevard, 4th Street or the Ramona Expressway may have both a comp claim and a claim against the other driver. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply and what the deadlines are.

items.title: Comp Is Not Always the Only Claim
items.desc: Workers' compensation is generally your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker or driver can be held separately responsible. An attorney can check whether a third party played a role in your injury.

items.title: Reporting and Retaliation Protections
items.desc: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and it is illegal for an employer to punish you for doing so. If you are worried about your job, a lawyer can explain those protections plainly.

items.title: Deadlines That Do Not Wait
items.desc: Third-party injury claims in California carry a two-year filing deadline, and evidence from a job site fades quickly. Connecting with an attorney early keeps every option on the table.

items.question: I was hurt in a Perris warehouse. Can I sue my employer?
items.answer: In most cases, no. California law makes workers' compensation the exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. However, if a staffing agency, a separate contractor on site, or the manufacturer of faulty equipment contributed to the injury, a separate claim against that third party may be possible. An attorney can review the facts and tell you which route applies.

items.question: I was driving for work on the Ramona Expressway when another driver hit me. What claims do I have?
items.answer: You may have two. Your injury happened on the job, so workers' compensation should cover medical care and part of your lost wages. Because another driver caused the crash, you may also bring a third-party claim against that driver within California's two-year deadline. The two claims interact, so it helps to have a lawyer coordinate them.

items.question: Does it cost anything to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney; we are not a law firm. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery. You can ask questions before deciding whether to move forward.
